title: fix(runtime,rest): advertise `mcp` only when it is actually serveable
body:
Fixes #4024.

## The bug

Both discovery producers gated `/mcp` on `isMcpServerEnabled()` alone. The dispatcher documented why that was safe:

> `declared === enforced` here is guaranteed by a LOCKSTEP … `os serve` auto-loads plugin-mcp from the SAME `isMcpServerEnabled()` flag that gates this advertisement, so whenever `/mcp` is advertised the handler is mounted (a key / token yields 401, never a 404/501). Kept flag-based on purpose — **`@objectstack/rest` advertises `mcp` from the identical single source (rest-server.ts), so the two discovery producers stay symmetric.**

The reasoning is correct about `os serve` and I want to be explicit that the CLI path was never broken: `packages/cli/package.json` declares `@objectstack/mcp`, `serve.ts:724` auto-pushes the capability, and the loader `import()`s it from inside the CLI package — so it resolves regardless of what the app depends on. `os dev` spawns `os serve --dev`, so it inherits that.

But the lockstep is a property of **the CLI**, not of the dispatcher, and the claimed symmetry with `@objectstack/rest` does not hold. `@objectstack/rest` has **no** `@objectstack/mcp` dependency, mounts **no** `/mcp` route, and performs **no** auto-load. So a host that embeds it without plugin-mcp advertised `/mcp` in `/discovery` and then got 501 from `domains/mcp.ts`.

Every *other* optional route in that table is service-presence gated (`hasUi`, `hasFiles`, `hasAnalytics`, `hasI18n`, …). `mcp` was the lone exception, and the exception is what broke.

This is a contract problem, not a tidiness one: `/discovery` is what a third-party client reads to decide what exists, and the objectui Integrations page renders its MCP connect card from this field.

## Reproduced

#4024 was filed as static analysis with the repro **explicitly listed as not done**. It reproduces. Flag on, service absent, old gate — the new pairing assertion fails with the defect stated verbatim:

```
AssertionError: discovery advertised mcp (true) while POST /mcp returned 501 — declared ≠ enforced
```

## The fix

Flag **and** serveable, on both producers.

- **Dispatcher** gates on the handler's *own* predicate — `typeof mcpSvc?.handleHttpRequest === 'function'`, byte-identical to what `handleMcpRequest` 501s on. Gating on mere service presence would still over-promise when a wrong-shaped service is registered.
- **`@objectstack/rest`** probes via the per-request kernel (shape) or the single-env `serviceExistsProvider` (existence) — the same two paths `resolveRegisteredServices` already uses for nav capability gates. I checked that `rest-api-plugin.ts` *always* wires the latter, so the gate is live in real deployments rather than decorative. When it genuinely cannot probe, it keeps the prior flag-only answer: "unknown" is not "absent", and hiding a working endpoint would be the opposite over-correction (fail-open, ADR-0057 D10).

`os serve` / `os dev` are unaffected — they load the plugin, so the service resolves and `/mcp` is still advertised.

## The seam that should have caught this

`route-parity.integration.test.ts` has carried an `mcp` opt-out in `stubServicesPlugin` since it was written, and **nothing ever passed it** — `bootServe()` was called with no args and with `{ notification: false }`, never `{ mcp: false }`. Its MCP test (*"MCP is advertised AND reachable"*) stubs the service in unconditionally, proving the lockstep only under the one condition where it cannot fail.

So the single capability whose advertisement was not service-presence gated was also the single one whose absence was never tested. The seam is now used.

Also added rest-side coverage, because the three existing `routes.mcp` tests construct `RestServer` with three args and therefore *all* take the unprobeable path — without new cases the rest half would have shipped with **no coverage at all**. New cases: absent → omitted, present → advertised, unprobeable → flag-only.

Each new assertion was verified to fail against the old gate and pass against the new one. The two "present" / "unprobeable" cases pass under both gates by design — they are guard rails against over-correction, not regression detectors, and I'm noting that rather than implying they bite.

## Testing

- runtime + rest **906 passed** (65 files)
- rest alone **494 passed** (34 files)
- `pnpm lint` clean; 0 type errors
- Changeset: `@objectstack/runtime` + `@objectstack/rest` patch

## Note on branching

This landed on a new branch rather than the session's designated `claude/global-actions-unreachable-rw7hpk`, whose PR (#4015) is merged. Separate issue, separate branch — say the word if you'd rather it be re-pointed.
